original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Price the integer transvection alphabet {X^t, Y^t : t nonzero} on B^k at the PR #4126 moment parameters, without using the three-bit quotient as a bill.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a new register identity escaping the three-register obstruction. This package does not build that identity. It answers the larger-alphabet question left open by the unit-shear supplier inequality, which is a different object on the same bit-mechanism track.
bottleneck_link: Side result. A rank-only pass for the single matrix B would matter only if the coefficient were legally one child and the same bound held for the powers a recurrence calls. The powers fail, and dropping the idle role removes the pass, so the selected exponent is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once the elementary-length classification and both role-count readings are checked. Do not open a third alphabet in this session.
evidence: Written length classification for every k, plus exact checks through B^24 of the recurrence, the word (X^2 Y^2)^k, the closed forms, the unit breadth-first control, and the strict moment comparison on rationals of denominator at most 8.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance for the proof writeup, the verifier, and the overlap selection.

open_questions.question: If a coefficient t=2 is one shift plus a unit shear, rather than one child or two unit children, does M(a)<1 still hold for B at W=2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The rank-only pass and the unit-alphabet failure are the two extremes. A legal shift price decides which side this alphabet lands on.
open_questions.first_step: Name one native operation that implements the shift, charge its rank and any dirty auxiliary, and recompute the two-role moment for the word that uses t=2.
open_questions.blocked_by: The rank-only model has no such native shift. Inventing one would be a new alphabet, not a corollary of this classification.
